Subject: FinTechCo - RTBF/deletion workflow follow-up

Hi Sarah — great to meet yesterday. Per our discovery call, wanted to capture the follow-ups and proposed next steps on data handling / RTBF so your compliance team can review.

Quick recap
- Scope: requests to delete PII and customer conversational data for end users (RTBF) coming from FinTechCo support/admin portal.
- Required: confirmation of purge timeline for primary data, treatment of backups/snapshots, and logging retention for audit.

Answers / suggestions from Redwood (initial)
- Primary data purge: Redwood can trigger a customer-specific purge pipeline that removes primary indexed user data and associated embeddings/derived artifacts within 72 hours of a validated RTBF request.
- Audit logs: access logs and generated request traces are retained separately for security/audit; default retention is 90 days but can be adjusted per contract. We can pseudonymize logs earlier on request.
- Backups & snapshots: we rely on cloud provider snapshots for backups. Immutable snapshots may require up to 30-90 days before provider-level garbage collection; we will surface the earliest possible purge timeline and document any vendor constraints.

Attachments: redwood-rtbf-overview.pdf (high-level workflow), proposed-maf.xlsx (proposed mutual action plan with milestones).

Next steps
1) Can you confirm whether FinTechCo requires complete provable deletion of backups or an attestation within a specific SLA (e.g., 30/45/90 days)?
2) Please confirm who from your compliance/infra teams we should loop in — I see you copied compliance@fintechco.com on follow-ups.
3) We’ll run an internal engineering checklist to enumerate provider-specific snapshot constraints and provide an expected purge timeline.

If that looks right I’ll coordinate with Mateo and our infra team and come back with a short FAQ for your compliance review.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah — thanks for the quick reply and for looping compliance in. A few concrete answers and the temporary controls we can offer while we validate provider constraints: 

Concrete timelines (initial estimates — engineering to confirm)
- Primary data purge: 72 hours after validated RTBF request (removes user profile, conversational records, embeddings, and derived artifacts from primary stores and search indexes).
- Logs/audit traces: default retention 90 days; we can offer pseudonymization at 30 days and permanent deletion at 90 days, or accelerate deletion as a contract term if required.
- Backups / snapshots: typical cloud snapshot GC windows vary by provider. For our hosted customers we’ve seen full deletion possible within 30 days for incremental backups, but immutable cold snapshots (VaultStore-style vendors) can be 45-90 days. We will confirm specifics with infra and the third-party vendor.

Interim mechanism:
- Account disable + quarantine: we can immediately disable the account and quarantine new writes, revoke live access tokens, and prevent further processing while deletion runs. This is available immediately on request.

Deliverables / next steps
1) I’ll attach a short engineering checklist (rtbf-eng-checklist.docx) and coordinate with Mateo to confirm snapshot vendor windows.
2) We can produce a deletion attestation template that provides an auditable record once the purge completes — our legal can sign off.
3) Please have your compliance team send the SOC2 / data flow questions to compliance@redwood.ai so we can respond systematically.

If you’re OK with that I’ll have Mateo join and we’ll aim to return with vendor-specific timelines by EOD Thu (Jun 11).

Best,
Camila

Hi team — looping in infra/ops (I will open a ticket with our infra team and ping VaultStore if FinTechCo confirms that vendor). A couple notes from infra perspective: 

- Snapshot immutability: Many long-term vendors enforce a legal hold/immutable snapshot policy which can delay physical deletion. For those, we can still remove customer-facing indexes and logical records immediately, and mark the snapshot for deletion at the vendor level; vendor GC can take 30-90 days.
- Attestation: We can provide a certified deletion attestation once logical purge completes and again after vendor confirms snapshot destruction. My proposal: offer a dual-attestation approach — (1) confirmation of logical purge within 72 hours, (2) final attestation within 45 days where possible (or vendor-confirmed window).
- Pricing/contract: if FinTechCo requires acceleration below typical vendor windows (e.g., guaranteed 30-day full deletion), we may need to formalize additional contractual terms covering vendor coordination effort and cert fees.

Camila — happy to draft the attestation language and the short FAQ for compliance. Sarah — would you like us to include a stub in the MAF for the attestation SLA?

Thanks,
